theme: The sword of judgment; Ezekiel’s wife dies, sign act
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 21:1-24:27. A sword is drawn against Jerusalem, a rusty pot boils on a fire, and Ezekiel’s wife dies at God’s command. Read chapter 24 slowly. It is one of the saddest passages in the prophets.
settingTheScene: It is now 588 BC, and the siege of Jerusalem is beginning. On the very day, Ezekiel, far away in Babylon, is told to write down the date. The rest of this section describes the sword of the LORD and the sins of the city. Chapter 24 ends the first main part of the book. God tells Ezekiel that his wife will die, and he is not to mourn publicly. His grief becomes a sign to the exiles of what will happen to them when the temple falls.
observation: “Behold, I am against you, and will draw my sword from its sheath” (21:3).
“A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished” (21:9).
“I will make you a ruin, ruin, ruin… until he comes, the one to whom the judgment belongs, and I will give it to him” (21:27).
“And I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none” (22:30).
“Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother” (23:2).
“Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem this very day” (24:2).
“Behold, I am about to take the delight of your eyes away from you at a stroke; yet you shall not mourn or weep” (24:16).
“So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my wife died” (24:18).
interpretation:
Chapter 21 shows the sword of the LORD, polished for slaughter. The king of Babylon stands at a fork in the road and uses divination to decide whether to attack Jerusalem or Rabbah. God directs the lot toward Jerusalem. It is a reminder that even pagan decisions serve God’s purpose. And the last line hints at hope: “until he comes, the one to whom the judgment belongs.” This is a messianic hint. The rightful king will come.

Chapter 22 lists the sins of the city: bloodshed, idolatry, contempt for parents, extortion from the sojourner, oppression of the fatherless and widow, profaning the Sabbath, adultery, bribery. The leaders are blamed: priests, princes, prophets, and people. Then comes the saddest verse: “I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none.” God was looking for an intercessor, someone like Moses. There was no one. The absence of a mediator is a deep need.

Chapter 23 tells the story of two sisters, Oholah (Samaria) and Oholibah (Jerusalem), who gave themselves to foreign lovers. It is a harsh allegory of political and religious unfaithfulness.

Chapter 24 begins with a boiling pot. The rusty pot, full of choice pieces of meat, is set on a fire until it is empty and burned clean. It shows Jerusalem under siege, with her bloodguilt cooked in her. Then comes the personal blow. God tells Ezekiel that his wife, “the delight of your eyes,” will die. He is told not to mourn publicly. The next day, he does as commanded. When the people ask why, he says that when the temple, “the delight of your eyes,” is taken, they too will be struck silent. His grief was a sign.

We should not skip past the cost to Ezekiel. He is a person with real feelings, who loves his wife. Prophetic ministry is not detached. It can mean personal loss. And in his silence, we hear the weight of the judgment.
connection: 1 Timothy 2:5 says, “There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.” Hebrews 7:25 says he always lives to make intercession. Isaiah 59:16 says God saw that there was no one to intercede, and his own arm brought salvation. Jesus stood in the breach on the cross. Romans 12:15 says to weep with those who weep. 1 Thessalonians 4:13 says we do not grieve as those who have no hope.
application:
Be someone who stands in the breach for others. Pray earnestly for a specific person, family, or situation.

Think about the cost to those who serve God faithfully, and pray for pastors and missionaries who have suffered loss.

Thank Jesus, the one mediator, who stood in the breach for you.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for standing in the breach for you.
Pray for someone you can stand in the breach for.
Ask him to keep you from indifference.
